In [[differential topology]], an area of mathematics, a '''neat submanifold''' of a [[manifold with boundary]] is a kind of "well-behaved" [[submanifold]].

To define this more precisely, first let

:<math>M</math> be a manifold with boundary, and
:<math>A</math> be a submanifold of <math>M</math>.

Then <math>A</math> is said to be a neat submanifold of <math>M</math> if it meets the following two conditions:<ref>{{citation|title=Lectures on Dynamical Systems, Structural Stability, and Their Applications|first=Kotik K.|last=Lee|publisher=World Scientific|year=1992|isbn=9789971509651|page=109|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=saQC-ZqEYj8C&pg=PA109}}.</ref>
*The boundary of <math>A</math> is a subset of the boundary of <math>M</math>. That is, <math>\partial A \subset \partial M</math>.{{dubious|date=September 2021}}
*Each point of <math>A</math> has a neighborhood within which  <math>A</math>'s embedding in <math>M</math> is equivalent to the embedding of a [[hyperplane]] in a higher-dimensional Euclidean space.

More formally, <math>A</math> must be [[Cover (topology)|covered]] by [[Manifold#Charts|charts]] <math>(U, \phi)</math> of <math>M</math> such that <math>A \cap U = \phi^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^m)</math> where <math>m</math> is the dimension {{nowrap|of <math>A</math>.}} For instance, in the category of [[smooth manifold]]s, this means that the embedding of <math>A</math> must also be smooth.
